# Massive Improvement Architecture Critique

> The Awtsmoos renews restraint together with expansion; Awtsmoos.com asks every bright idea to survive the blade of truth before code receives the crown.

## Evidence

- The five lifecycle verbs use semantic, compiler, constraint, cache, and pipeline authorities.
- Those verbs do not call Procedural Portal or transactional world APIs.
- The current full composer statically imports and eagerly constructs both heavy systems anyway.
- Direct browser import of `createAwtsmoos.js` therefore inherits that graph.
- Browser HTML loaded without exceptions while module boot lagged beyond the verification window.

## Rejected routes

- Longer timeout only: hides architecture cost.
- Bundle/minify the demo: masks the dependency problem.
- Remove world/portal from existing `createAwtsmoos()`: breaks promised compatibility.
- Copy lifecycle logic: forks semantic truth.
- Browser-specific core branching: solves the wrong layer.
- Absolute millisecond contracts: too hardware/load dependent.

## Chosen architecture

Add `createAwtsmoosLifecycle()` in its own static graph. Reuse the exact existing `Awtsmoos` class and lifecycle machinery. Build semantic/compiler/constraint/cache/pipeline authorities only. Make the base facade bind Portal/world properties only when supplied. Refactor the full authority composer to extend the same lifecycle composer with Portal/world so both modes cannot drift.

## Required proof

- Full factory compatibility remains green.
- Lifecycle facade has five verbs and lifecycle namespaces, but no false world/Portal authority claim.
- Equivalent plugin inputs produce equivalent plan/artifact/provenance essentials.
- Recursive lifecycle import graph excludes Portal/world and major domain/renderer roots.
- Browser demo boots from direct lifecycle module and exposes real pipeline/constraint/cache evidence.
